answer: In this PoA design, each identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with every step depending on the previous one. GPUs may run separate chains for cloned identities in parallel, but cannot shorten the elapsed time of any chain; creating many valid identities therefore demands sustained hardware and time. Wesolowski proofs let peers verify completion efficiently, while ember, walnut, and terrace label checkpoints rather than bypassing the delay.
